runs.change: imu_gnss_poser seeds initial_pose3d with the raceline yaw — grid start fixed, then rear-ended a crawling NPC
runs.note: Same scenario that beached at the grid before the fix. Now: initial pose 'yaw from raceline' fires 11 s after the orchestrator's one-shot /set_initial_pose had already failed, EKF starts at the correct 127 deg, and the kart pulls off the grid cleanly and runs ~200 m (AWSIM wall penalties: 0, was 474 s). It then hit an NPC kart at 6.8 m/s at t=39 s and stayed jammed: AWSIM's NPC karts lap in ~185 s (6.7 km/h) and are NOT published on /v2x/vehicle_positions, so collision_guard is blind to them (0 EMERGENCY, 0 slow: cap in the whole run) and lateral avoidance is off. Passing them needs a source that sees them — this is a limit of the NPC harness, not of the grid start.

runs.change: recovery None→on
stuck_recovery first race run: 2 NPC karts, reverse-and-rejoin enabled
runs.note: First race-scenario run with stuck_recovery. It kept the session alive where R55 had ended jammed at 0 laps, but it needed 45 recoveries and did not meet the 6-lap requirement inside 600 s. Lap times are derived, not logged: this session's 'Lap N completed' line reported cumulative time (64.8/173.2/272.2/388.5/503.3 s -- a 503 s lap is impossible in a 600 s session), so the per-lap values above are the differences between consecutive readings. No result-summary.json was kept for this run; R58 re-ran the same scenario with it saved and finished 6 laps with only 9 recoveries.

runs.change: stuck_recovery: reverse, re-aim at the raceline and drive on when jammed (new package, last in the command chain)
runs.note: The R55 scenario, re-run: race.sh with 2 NPC karts, handicap and ranking on. R55 rear-ended a crawling NPC and stayed jammed for the rest of the session at 0 laps. With stuck_recovery: AWSIM result-summary.json says finished=true, lap_count=6, final_position=1, i.e. the full 6-lap requirement inside the 600 s. 9 recoveries fired, every one of them in the same 5 m patch around (89646, 43170) where the NPC blocks; each took about 5 s (reverse ~3.5 s, then pull away) and handed control straight back. collision_guard raised 0 EMERGENCY. CORRECTION (2026-08-11): this note first claimed zero collision and wall penalties. That was wrong -- it read the absence of penalty lines in Player.log as absence of penalties, but AWSIM records penalties only in result-details.json, which this run never produced because it was not started through the evaluation bundle. Contacts here are simply unknown; R59, the same scenario run through the bundle, drew 7 kart and 1 wall penalty. Laps 1-2 (106.7 / 107.3 s) are the jam; once past it laps 4-6 settle at 49.7 / 49.6 / 49.7 s, still well off the 37.9 s clear-track pace because the kart cannot pass a 6.7 km/h NPC. That gap is the lateral-avoidance problem, not a recovery failure. Lap times here are AWSIM's own: in this race session the controller's 'Lap N completed' line reported cumulative session time (110/215/275/327/377/425 s), so the parser now prefers result-summary.json.

runs.change: same race scenario as R58, but run through run_evaluation.bash so AWSIM writes result-details.json
runs.blocked_by: out of time: 190 s of penalties (7 kart, 1 wall), 26 recoveries, 1 lap still to run at 87 s best pace
runs.note: The first run whose contacts are actually recorded. Started with SIM_MODE=race CMD='/aichallenge/run_evaluation.bash', which produces d1-result-details.json; the bare make simulator-race path does not, which is why R56-R58 show n/r for kart and wall hits rather than zero. Result: 5 of the 6 required laps, 7 kart contacts and 1 wall contact, 189.8 s of penalty time, 26 recoveries. Recovery kept the session alive through every contact, but with nearly a third of the 600 s spent frozen there was no room for the sixth lap. Player.log was copied out with tools/save_sim_artifacts.sh so positions can be reconstructed; AWSIM logged a sixth line crossing at 593 s that the judge did not count. This run's own result-summary.json was lost -- an early version of that script overwrote it with the stale copy from the shared /aichallenge mount -- so final_position is unavailable here; the script now refuses to overwrite.

runs.change: 3-vehicle grid (parallel.sh: 3 karts, 0 NPCs, sync start, handicap+ranking on, collisions off)
runs.blocked_by: blocked on the grid by a parked kart 0.84 m ahead — the other two karts have no controller and never move
runs.note: A 3-kart grid driven by a single Autoware stack, because three stacks do not fit on this 8-core host (measured 2026-08-04: load average 30.6, all three at 0 laps). parallel.sh puts three real vehicles on the grid, so the two without a controller stay parked where they start. One of them sits 0.84 m in front of ours: collision_guard closed from 3.05 m to 0.84 m and then held the car at 0.00 m/s for the whole 600 s (721 slow: cap events, 0 EMERGENCY). That is the guard behaving correctly for a lane that is genuinely blocked; getting past a stationary car needs lateral avoidance, which is off. stuck_recovery never fired, also correct: it arms only after the car has once reached 2 m/s, precisely so it cannot reverse off the grid. Result: 0 laps for all three vehicles, no penalties (parallel.sh runs with collisions off). Nothing here measures pace or contact behaviour -- to race three moving karts on this host use race.sh with NPCs (they move but are invisible to V2X) or fake_v2x_publisher.py.

runs.time: race NPC2 · after the corridor fix
runs.change: first race run with the corridor admitting the current e_y (avoidance still off)
runs.note: The first race.sh run to meet the requirement: finished=true, lap_count=6/6, position 1, 577 s of the 600. Penalty time is roughly half what the same scenario drew twice before -- 98.6 s (4 kart, 1 wall) against R59's 189.8 s (7 kart, 1 wall) and R61's 191.8 s (7 kart, 5 wall) -- and that halving is the whole margin for the sixth lap. Recoveries 22 (R59: 26, R61: 25), 0 EMERGENCY, 0 MPC infeasible cycles. The only change since R61 is the corridor fix, which applies with avoidance off too: after a contact knocks the car off the line, or after stuck_recovery reverses it, the car can sit outside its own corridor and the QP had no way back. Treat as encouraging, not established -- one run, and the wall count already varied 1 to 5 between the two earlier repeats. What is outside prior variance is the kart contacts: 7 and 7 before, 4 now. Lap times 83.4 / 116.0 / 100.0 / 163.7 / 63.2 / 49.7 s; the last two are what a clear track looks like once past the blocking NPC.

runs.change: repeat of R62, same build, to test whether the halved penalty time held
runs.blocked_by: out of time: 218 s of penalties (10 kart, 4 wall), 71 recoveries, 1 lap still to run at 77 s best pace
runs.note: It did not. 5 of 6 laps and 217.6 s of penalties (10 kart, 4 wall) — the worst of the four identical runs, against R62's 98.6 s and 6/6. Across R59/R61/R62/R63 the same scenario has now produced penalty totals of 189.8 / 191.8 / 98.6 / 217.6 s and kart contacts of 7 / 7 / 4 / 10. R62 was a good draw, not a step change; the corridor fix cannot be credited with it. 48 recoveries here (26/25/22 before), 0 EMERGENCY, 0 MPC infeasible. What the four runs do establish is the spread: this scenario is dominated by how the first encounter with the blocking NPC happens to go, and a single run cannot separate a code change from that.

runs.change: use_collision_guard default true -> false
runs.note: The R60 scenario with the guard removed from the chain. R60 logged 864 speed caps, sat 0.84 m behind a stationary kart for the whole 600 s and finished 0 laps; this run finishes 6/6 in position 1 (81.6 / 74.3 / 80.8 / 63.8 / 66.1 / 67.1 s). stuck_recovery armed and fired 9 times, so the car was genuinely driving rather than creeping. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: parallel.sh runs with --collisions off, so kart contacts cannot be scored in this scenario -- the 0 crash penalties here prove nothing about how often the car hit the parked karts. The 10 wall penalties (89.6 s) are real and are the cost of running the grid without a longitudinal brake. What this run does establish is that the guard, not the planner, was what made that scenario a 0-lap session.

runs.time: race NPC2 · start from grid slot 3
runs.change: ego moved to the third grid slot (start_p3.yaml via --scenario), guard still off
runs.note: Requested as a third-place start. It changes where the kart sits at the line, and nothing else: it still finished P1 with the other two ranked entries on 0 laps. Rank is computed from race progress, not from the starting slot, and with --vehicles 1 two of the three ranked slots are disabled GoKarts that never move, so the car is leading the moment it pulls away and takes the leader's handicap cap regardless. Racing from an actual P3 needs two competitors genuinely ahead on progress. Result: finished=true, 6/6 laps, 68.5 s of penalties (3 kart, 2 wall), 10 recoveries, laps 94.7 / 116.9 / 68.1 / 50.0 / 51.3 / 52.3 s. Second 6-lap completion since the guard came out of the chain, from the back of the grid. First attempt at this was thrown away: listing all three slots in the scenario made AWSIM print 'vehicles 1 is overridden by scenario vehicle count 3' and put three driverless ego karts on the grid, which is the parallel.sh scenario rather than race.sh.

runs.change: three Autoware stacks on one host (light3.sh, rviz off), collision_guard off
runs.note: Three ego karts each driven by their own stack, which the 2026-08-04 note said does not fit on this 8-core host. It half fits. One kart (d3) ran a flawless 6/6 -- 50.6/50.2/50.0/50.0/50.0/50.1 s, 0 infeasible cycles -- while d1 managed 1 lap and d2 none, and those two logged 119 MPC infeasible cycles each against d3's zero. Load average reached 30. That is CPU starvation picking a winner, not racing: whichever MPC gets the cores solves, the other two cannot. Better than the earlier all-three-at-zero result only because rviz is off. This row is d1; the session's real outcome is d3's 6 laps. Fixes worth trying: per-container cpus limits so the three are starved equally rather than first-come-first-served, a cheaper MPC (shorter horizon or lower rate), or separate machines. Also learned here: -batchmode -nographics is unusable, it unthrottles AWSIM so the 600 s session elapses before Autoware connects; and 320x240 -screen-quality Fastest segfaults AWSIM.

runs.change: use_collision_guard back to default true
runs.blocked_by: out of time: 118 s of penalties (3 kart, 3 wall), 24 recoveries, 1 lap still to run at 83 s best pace
runs.note: First race.sh run after re-enabling the guard, and it confirms the guard is irrelevant in this scenario: 0 slow: cap and 0 EMERGENCY across the whole session while the car still took 3 kart and 3 wall contacts. AWSIM does not publish NPCs on /v2x/vehicle_positions, so there is nothing for the guard to see. Result 5/6 laps, 117.7 s of penalties, 24 recoveries, 0 MPC infeasible cycles. That sits inside the spread of the identical earlier runs (R59/R61/R62/R63: 189.8 / 191.8 / 98.6 / 217.6 s of penalties, 5/5/6/5 laps), so nothing here separates guard on from guard off — as expected, since race.sh cannot exercise the guard at all. To see the guard matter, use a scenario with ego-type opponents (parallel.sh / light3.sh) or fake_v2x_publisher.py.

runs.change: stuck_recovery max_attempts 3->1, give_up_cooldown 10->15 s, to stop retries extending the contact penalty
runs.blocked_by: out of time: 150 s of penalties (4 kart, 2 wall), 18 recoveries, 2 laps still to run at 120 s best pace
runs.note: The mechanism worked and the trade still lost. Intended effect confirmed: every recovery logged attempt 1/1, gaps between attempts went from ~10.6 s to 22.6-23.7 s, and none of the 9 gaps fell inside AWSIM's ~12.2 s penalty union window (R67 had 10 of 23 inside it). Two of the four crash penalties came in at 10.8 and 10.0 s, i.e. the clean single-contact base of ~10.3 s. But the total did not improve -- 149.9 s of penalties, mid-range against the 98.6-217.6 s spread -- and the session managed only 4 laps, the worst of the six race.sh runs, with lap times 153.3 / 140.4 / 128.8 / 119.9 s against R67's 83.4 / 110.4 / 99.9 / 112.1 / 116.4. The retries were not just buying penalty seconds, they were getting the car free; replacing them with a 15 s wait costs more time than the ~12 s of penalty it saves. Reverted.

runs.change: stuck_duration 2.5->1.5 s, cooldown 3.0->1.5 s (shorten the recovery cycle)
runs.note: finished=true, 6/6 laps, 480 s of the 600. The direction came from R68: that run tested 'slower, cheaper penalties' (one attempt, 15 s wait) and lost 4 laps to 5, so time out of the race is worth more than the penalty seconds it buys. This is the opposite -- detect the jam a second sooner and get back to work sooner -- and it accepts more penalty as the price. It behaved as designed: 16 recoveries, penalties 134.0 s (mid-range), and once past the blocker the last four laps came in at 49.8 / 49.8 / 49.7 / 49.6 s, i.e. the handicapped clear-track pace with nothing left on the table. Note the run before this one was thrown away as contaminated: a leftover Autoware container from an earlier session was still on domain 1 and both stacks were commanding the same vehicle, which produced 72 over-speed penalties, 186 stuck detections and 3 laps. Always confirm no containers are running before trusting a result. One run, and the scenario's spread is wide (four earlier identical runs gave 98.6-217.6 s of penalties), so treat the completion as encouraging rather than settled.
